ABOUT / MANNY MAYORGA

I like software that explains itself.

I’m a developer in Arizona interested in the seam between systems and interfaces—the place where technical decisions become something a person can feel.

Rough at Sea is where I document that work honestly: the useful patterns, the wrong turns, and the moment a simpler architecture becomes the better one.

WORKING PRINCIPLES

01

Clarity is a technical feature.

Names, boundaries, interfaces, and documentation all shape whether a system can be understood and changed safely.

02

Complexity needs to earn rent.

A sophisticated solution is worthwhile only when it creates proportionate value. Deleting infrastructure can be architecture work.

03

Design belongs in the implementation.

Good front-end work connects visual intent to responsive behavior, accessibility, performance, and maintainable code.

NOW

Building the ship
as I sail it.

Learning Static architecture, content systems, and expressive interfaces.

Writing Practical notes about decisions rather than victory laps.

Exploring Small tools that make complicated work feel legible.

Keep a weather eye open.

Occasional notes on code, craft, and changing course.
